key_highlights: ASX opened lower on Wall Street sell-off and bond-market pressure but closed flat as miners offset oil-stock weakness; IDP plunged
RBA signals further rate hikes as OECD warns Australia will struggle to bring inflation below 3%, squeezing household spending
Aussie flash PMI sags, reinforcing softening domestic demand narrative
Fuel price fears mount as global oil buffers dry up; oil prices jumped intraday before easing
Gold miners active: Critical Resources surged on Suriname grab, Aurum raised $52.5M for West Africa, WA Jupiter rare-earths offtake progress
Qantas/Jetstar industrial action escalates with staff waiving baggage fees; Qantas confirms Sydney-New York non-stop
Federal and state governments face rising debt pressures; energy-cost policy debate intensifies
El Niño 'Godzilla' event threatens agricultural output and food prices
Property market softens: rising listings and falling demand push prices lower

sectors.trend: Miners rose to support the ASX; gold miners (Critical Resources, Aurum) and rare-earths (WA Jupiter) saw positive catalysts. Oil stocks struggled on intraday volatility. Chinese property recovery question adds uncertainty for iron ore demand.
sectors.implications: Gold and critical-minerals names offer relative strength; iron ore exposure (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) faces headwind from Chinese property ambiguity. Rare-earths offtake deals support small-cap miners.

sectors.trend: RBA rate-hike cycle continues, supporting net interest margins but squeezing household borrowing. Debt cliff for governments raises sovereign-credit concerns. Qantas/Jetstar strikes pressure transport-linked credit.
sectors.implications: Big Four banks (CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX) benefit from higher rates but face rising credit-risk from stressed households. Government debt trajectory is a medium-term overhang.

sectors.trend: Oil prices jumped then eased; fuel-price fears as global buffers dry up. Power companies backed to pass EV-charger costs to consumers. Data-centre energy demand threatens net-zero targets. Energy-cost policy dispute between Labor and Coalition.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, SXG.AX, AWE.AX face cost-push inflation risk. EV-charger cost pass-through may pressure consumer sentiment. Energy transition spending accelerates.

sectors.trend: Syngenis gains precision-medicine firepower. Migrant doctors filling GP gaps highlights structural supply issues. OpenAI Medicare breach raises data-security concerns.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, SYG.AX benefit from structural demand. Data-breach risk is a reputational tail-risk for health-tech integrations.

sectors.trend: Qantas and Jetstar industrial action disrupts airline operations. RBA hikes squeeze discretionary spending. Property prices falling on rising listings. El Niño threatens food supply.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces operational and cost pressure from strikes. WES.AX, WTW.AX under margin pressure. REITs (GPW.AX, SPG.AX) face falling property valuations.

sectors.trend: $16B Aussie tech firm faces China-link controversy. AI infrastructure boom (TXN, Prosus) drives global tech rally. OpenAI Medicare breach highlights AI governance gaps.
sectors.implications: ASX-listed tech (W1.AX, XRO.AX) may face scrutiny on China exposure. AI infrastructure theme supports global tech but raises cybersecurity risk for AU firms.

key_themes: Sticky inflation and RBA rate-hike cycle pressuring household balance sheets
Commodity volatility: oil buffers drying, gold miners active, iron ore demand uncertain
Industrial action in aviation sector (Qantas, Jetstar)
China property recovery question affecting ASX miners

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate-hike cycle and sticky inflation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight rate-sensitive financials; underweight rate-sensitive REITs and property; monitor CPI prints

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fuel-price spike from drying global oil buffers
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge transport and logistics exposure; monitor A$ oil and Brent spreads
Watch sovereign credit ratings; favour banks with strong capital buffers
Monitor food-inflation data; consider agribusiness hedges
Reduce QAN.AX exposure; monitor strike duration and resolution
Diversify mining exposure away from pure iron-ore; favour gold and critical minerals

opportunities.rationale: Active capital raises and offtake deals signal sector momentum; gold benefits from rate-hike uncertainty and geopolitical risk

opportunities.recommendation: Selective bank exposure on NIM expansion
opportunities.rationale: RBA hikes support margins; CBA and NAB best positioned with strong capital and diversified lending
GP supply gaps and precision-medicine ventures support long-term sector growth

defensive_moves.rationale: Falling prices, rising listings, and higher rates create a triple headwind for property valuations

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim Qantas exposure pending strike resolution
defensive_moves.rationale: Industrial action escalates with fee waivers; operational disruption and cost pressure near-term
Drying oil buffers and El Niño create upward pressure on transport and food costs

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure from RBA rate-hike expectations, sticky inflation, and global bond-market volatility. Miners provide partial support. Qantas strikes and fuel-price fears add near-term noise. Expect range-bound trading with downside bias.
market_outlook.long_term: Medium-term outlook cautious: household spending squeezed by higher rates, property market cooling, and government debt concerns. Gold, healthcare, and critical minerals offer relative strength. Recovery hinges on inflation turning and RBA pivoting. Chinese property trajectory is the key external variable for iron ore.
